evidence: src/application/advance-order-use-case.ts: validateExecute(status: unknown) throws DomainError("VALIDATION", "Query parameter 'status' must be a valid order status") when !isOrderStatus(status)
src/application/list-orders-use-case.ts: execute(status: unknown) has the identical guard and message: DomainError("VALIDATION", "Query parameter 'status' must be a valid order status")
src/application/advance-order-use-case.ts: execute() repeats the isOrderStatus check inline with a different message, "Unknown order status", and does not call validateExecute
src/application/get-stock-levels-use-case.ts: maps products to StockLevelDto inline, while order use cases go through toOrderDto in order-mapper.ts; StockLevelDto is declared in order-dto.ts
parsedVerdict.reasoning: Most of the module is cohesive. Each order use case loads or creates an Order, persists it and returns it through the shared toOrderDto mapper. However, the order-status validation rule is not kept in one place. AdvanceOrderUseCase has a public validateExecute(status) method that copies the guard in ListOrdersUseCase.execute word for word, including the same error message: "Query parameter 'status' must be a valid order status". execute() is the only entry point in AdvanceOrderUseCase that uses its own inline isOrderStatus check, with a different message ("Unknown order status"). So the status-validation rule now exists in three places with two different messages, and one of them refers to an HTTP "query parameter", which is a transport concern, inside an application use case. This is the kind of duplicated rule the rubric marks as a fail. A smaller point: StockLevelDto lives in order-dto.ts, and GetStockLevelsUseCase maps products to DTOs inline rather than through a mapper the way the order use cases do. That weakens the module's file boundaries a little, but on its own it isn't enough to fail.

violations.message: validateExecute repeats ListOrdersUseCase's order-status validation word for word, including the query-parameter wording, while execute() checks status a third way with a different message. The status-validation rule should live in one place.

The status guard in execute() (isOrderStatus check with the message "Query parameter 'status' must be a valid order status") also appears in AdvanceOrderUseCase.validateExecute, so the rule is duplicated.
